title: Finite exceptional-curve count and strict decrease after a target point blowup
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism between integral regular Noetherian schemes of dimension $2$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Assume $f$ is birational, meaning that it restricts to an isomorphism between dense open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $U_f\subseteq Y$ be the union of the open subschemes over which $f$ is an isomorphism. Define $B(f)$ to be the set of irreducible closed subsets $C\subset X$ of dimension $1$ for which $f(C)$ consists of one point [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Then $Y\setminus U_f$ is a finite set of closed points $y$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}=2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], $B(f)$ is finite, and $B(f)=\varnothing$ if and only if $f$ is an isomorphism. If $y\notin U_f$, $b:Y'=\operatorname{Bl}_yY\to Y$ is the blowup of the reduced closed point [def-nagata-global-blowup], and $g:X\to Y'$ is a proper birational morphism with $f=b\circ g$ and $Y'$ integral regular Noetherian of dimension $2$, then $B(g)\subsetneq B(f)$, with both sets regarded as sets of closed subsets of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R (resolve-lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), first proof paragraph: the finite induction measure and its strict decrease, whose details the source omits.

proof.text: By [def-pc-integral-scheme, lem-sc-scheme-sober], $X$ and $Y$ are reduced irreducible schemes with unique generic points. The dense opens in the birationality hypothesis contain these points; the given isomorphism identifies their local rings. Thus $f$ is birational in the precise sense required by [lem-sfb-normal-modification-codimension-one]. Its source is reduced and its target is Noetherian, so that statement applies. Regularity makes each local ring regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme]; in dimension one it is a DVR by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. Clauses (1) and (2) of the modification criterion therefore put every point of local dimension zero or one into $U_f$. Also, [rem-pc-regular-normal] makes every local ring of $Y$ normal. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] and the chain definition [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], every local dimension is at most $2$, since $\dim Y=2$. Consequently every $y\in S:=Y\setminus U_f$ has $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}=2$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R (lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), first paragraph; varieties.tex Tag 0BFP (lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1), clauses (1), (2); algebra.tex Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr).

proof.text: The set $S$ is closed, since $U_f$ is open. Every $y\in S$ is a closed point of $Y$: if a distinct point $z$ were a specialization of $y$, a length-two chain of generalizations starting at $y$, supplied by [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], could be prefixed with $z$. The closures of its four points would give a length-three chain of irreducible closed subsets in $Y$, contrary to $\dim Y=2$. Here distinct points have distinct closures by the uniqueness in [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite] to the Noetherian scheme $Y$ and its closed subset $S$. It follows that $S$ is finite, proving the first assertion, including when $S$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, first paragraph, omitted finiteness detail; properties.tex Tag 02IZ (lemma-codimension-local-ring) and Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components).

proof.text: Put $Z=f^{-1}(S)$ as a closed subset of $X$. It is proper: the generic point of $X$ maps to the generic point of $Y$, which lies in $U_f$ by Step 1. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], $Z$ has finitely many irreducible components $D_1,\ldots,D_t$, each closed in $X$. Every $D_i$ has dimension at most one. Indeed, any chain of length two inside this proper irreducible closed subset could be extended by $X$, which is irreducible, to a chain of length three in $X$, contradicting [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $\dim X=2$. The continuous image $f(D_i)$ is irreducible and is contained in the finite set of closed points $S$. Such a subset is a singleton: otherwise partition it into a point and its nonempty complement, both relatively closed since $S$ is finite and all its points are closed. Thus each one-dimensional $D_i$ belongs to $B(f)$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, first paragraph, omitted finiteness detail: components of the inverse image of the bad-point set; properties.tex Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components).

proof.text: Conversely, if $C\in B(f)$ and $f(C)=\{y\}$, then $y\notin U_f$: over $U_f$ the entire morphism is an isomorphism, so its fibre is a singleton, whereas a one-dimensional irreducible closed subset cannot be a singleton. Hence $C\subseteq Z$. A finite irreducible-component cover of $Z$ contains $C$ in some $D_i$, by irreducibility. This containment is equality. Otherwise a length-one chain inside $C$ (which exists because $\dim C=1$), followed by $D_i$ and then $X$, would have length three. Thus $B(f)$ is exactly the set of one-dimensional components of $Z$, a subset of the finite list in Step 3. This proves finiteness of $B(f)$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, first paragraph: expand the assertion that there are finitely many curves in fibres, using the finite component cover from Step 3.

proof.text: Suppose $B(f)=\varnothing$. Step 4 shows that every $D_i$ has dimension zero. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] each $D_i$ has a unique generic point $\xi_i$. If there were another point $z\in D_i$, its closure would be a proper nonempty irreducible closed subset of $D_i$ (otherwise $z$ would be a second generic point), a chain of length one. Thus $D_i=\{\xi_i\}$, and $Z$ is finite. Every fibre above $S$ is consequently finite. The local rings of $Y$ are normal by Step 1, so clause (3) of [lem-sfb-normal-modification-codimension-one] puts every point of $S$ into $U_f$. Hence $S=\varnothing$, $U_f=Y$, and $f$ is an isomorphism. Conversely, an isomorphism has singleton fibres and contracts no one-dimensional closed subset, so $B(f)=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, first paragraph, base case of the induction; varieties.tex Tag 0BFP (lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1), clause (3).

proof.text: Now assume the factorization $f=b\circ g$ in the statement. For $C\in B(g)$, the set $C$ is still an irreducible closed subset of $X$ of dimension one and $f(C)=b(g(C))$ is a singleton. Therefore $C\in B(f)$, proving $B(g)\subseteq B(f)$. It remains to exhibit a curve that is contracted by $f$ and not by $g$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, first paragraph: non-strict containment of the contracted-curve sets follows from the factorization.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $\mathfrak m$ for its maximal ideal. Step 1 gives $\dim A=2$, and $A$ is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The canonical map $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ is flat and induces the identity on the local ring at its closed point by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. Its pullback of the reduced point $y$ is defined by $\mathfrak m$. By [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map, thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], the blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ identifies over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_Y Y'$. Taking its fibre at $\mathfrak m$ identifies it with the fibre $E=Y'\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ of $b$, by the associativity universal property of fibre products; the residue fields agree since the local map at the closed point is the identity. By [lem-sfb-local-surface-maximal-blowup-geometry] this fibre is $\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(y)}$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] its underlying space is the closed subset $b^{-1}(y)\subset Y'$.

source.place: Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), clause (1), localized at y; divisors.tex Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up).

proof.text: The space $E$ is irreducible and has more than one point. To check this directly, use the standard cover in [def-sc-p1-standard]: the two charts are spectra of the domains $\kappa(y)[t]$ and $\kappa(y)[s]$, so are irreducible by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Their intersection is the nonempty spectrum of $\kappa(y)[t,t^{-1}]$. Two irreducible open subsets with nonempty intersection have irreducible union: any nonempty open in either chart meets their intersection, and any two nonempty opens therefore meet there. In the first chart the distinct prime ideals $(0)$ and $(t)$ give distinct points. Thus $E$ is a nonsingleton irreducible closed subset of $Y'$. It is proper because $b$ is birational and its generic point maps to the generic point of $Y$, not to the closed point $y$. Here birationality of $b$ also follows directly from $f=b g$ and the dense-open isomorphism away from $y$ supplied by [lem-sfb-regular-point-blowup-geometry].

source.place: Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), clause (1): elementary properties of its projective-line exceptional fibre; Tag 0C5R, first paragraph.

proof.text: The map $g$ is surjective: it is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and its image contains a dense open by the assumed birationality, so the image is all of $Y'$. The closed subset $F=g^{-1}(|E|)\subset X$ is proper, since $|E|$ is proper and $g$ is surjective. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] it has finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_r$. Their images under the proper map $g$ are closed and cover $|E|$. Irreducibility of $|E|$ forces one image $g(C_j)$ to be all of $|E|$. As in Step 3, any proper irreducible closed subset of the surface $X$ has dimension at most one. Moreover $C_j$ cannot have dimension zero: by [lem-sc-scheme-sober] the dimension-zero argument of Step 5 would make it a singleton, contradicting its nonsingleton image $|E|$. Therefore $\dim C_j=1$. Since $b(|E|)=\{y\}$, we have $f(C_j)=\{y\}$, whereas $g(C_j)=|E|$ is not a point. Thus $C_j\in B(f)\setminus B(g)$, which proves the strict containment together with Step 6.

Source check: Stacks 0C5R first paragraph, whose omitted details ('Some details omitted') the delivery supplies; 0C5R's 'codim-1 points of V' should read 'of Y', and 0BFP is the intended reference. All nine steps hold. Steps 1-2: birationality is matched to 0BFP-node via sober generic points; clauses (1) and (2) apply, with the DVR property from lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr. The chain lemma gives local dimension at most 2, a specialization would give a length-3 chain, so every bad point is closed and the bad set is finite by noetherian-closed-points-finite. Steps 3-4: Z=f^-1(S) is a proper subset with finitely many components of dimension at most 1, and B(f) is exactly its one-dimensional components. Step 5: B(f) empty makes the components singletons, so fibres are finite, and 0BFP(3) with regular-implies-normal gives S empty. Step 7: flat localization c (spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism (1)-(3)) plus nagata flat base change identify the fibre of b with the exceptional fibre of Bl_m Spec A, which local-surface-maximal-blowup-geometry says is P^1. Steps 8-9: P^1 is irreducible with at least two points, and |E| is a proper subset via regular-point-blowup-geometry. g is closed with dense image, hence surjective; a component C_j of g^-1|E| maps onto |E|, has dimension exactly 1, and lies in B(f) but not B(g). The argument avoids the source's 'maps isomorphically' claim. Edge cases checked: f an isomorphism; single blowup with g=id; several bad points; zero-dimensional fibre components; finite or imperfect residue fields; no excellence or catenarity assumed. Duplicate search (contracted curve, B(f), exceptional curve; point-blowup-fibre-defects, trf modification nodes, lem-per-surface-point-blowup-geometry) found none, so same_as [] stands.
